t: This is 12A Kensington Palace Gardens, a building commissioned by Samuel Morton Peto. Peto was an English entrepreneur, civil engineer and railway developer, and for more than twenty years a Member of Parliament. His firm built many of London's major buildings and monuments, including the Reform Club, the Lyceum Theatre, Nelson's Column and the replacement Houses of Parliament. Those commissions brought him great wealth, and the scale of his operations made him the world's largest employer. So the person who put up this house was someone who had helped build much of London itself.
